Get started with glyfp

glyfp.Rmd

The glyfp package provides a separate function for each structural fingerprint or pretrained glycan representation. Each returns a list of named vectors, one per input glycan, and exposes only options relevant to its method. Inputs can be glyrepr structure vectors or text in formats supported by glyparse.

Choose a method

Function Coordinates Source of features
fp_motif_binary() Presence/absence; 3,173 dimensions by default Fixed glydb motif dictionary
fp_motif_count() Overlapping occurrences; same dimensions Same fixed dictionary
fp_circular_binary() / fp_circular_count() 2,048 binary / count bins by default Residue-centered WL neighborhoods, radii 0–2 by default
fp_residue_pair() 2,048 binary bins by default; optional counts Endpoint environments plus graph distances
fp_sweetnet() 128 pretrained features SweetNet v2 by default; legacy v1 also supported
fp_glycangt() 768 pretrained graph Transformer features Large mask-35 model; local checkpoint required
fp_gifflar() 384 pretrained molecular graph features Species model; automatic verified download

Migrating existing calls

The former glycan_fingerprint() interface has been replaced by these functions. For example, replace glycan_fingerprint(x, "substructure_count", max_size = 2) with fp_motif_count(x, max_size = 2), and glycan_fingerprint(x, "sweetnet") with fp_sweetnet(x). Default calls glycan_fingerprint(x) become fp_motif_binary(x). The resulting vectors and defaults are unchanged.

max_size, motif_dict and unknown belong to the two motif functions. Only fp_sweetnet() and fp_gifflar() accept cache_dir and download. For GlycanGT, pass the required local checkpoint and omit any former download = FALSE argument. All fingerprint functions accept na_action; embedding functions always reject unknown tokens.

Every method processes complete structures. Specify concrete residues, all linkage positions and anomers, substituent positions, and the reducing-end alpha/beta state. For example, Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1- is complete; Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc leaves the reducing-end state unknown and is rejected. Validation inspects normalized glyrepr graph fields for text and object inputs. Empty substituent fields mean no modification, not unknown chemistry. Alditols and unresolved floating components/substituents are outside scope. Missing inputs (NA) are supported separately from uncertain structures.

Substructure fingerprints 

library(glyfp)
a <- c("Galb3Galb3Galb-", "Galb-")
b <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
fp_a <- fp_motif_count(a)
fp_b <- fp_motif_count(b)
lengths(fp_a)
#> [1] 3173 3173
stopifnot(identical(c(fp_a, fp_b),
                   fp_motif_count(c(a, b))))

With the default motif_dict = "fixed", the same glycan receives the same coordinates alone, in another batch, or in another order. Other inputs never redefine its dictionary. Text parsing is delegated to glyparse; equivalent objects yield the same values.

objects <- glyparse::auto_parse(a)
stopifnot(identical(fp_motif_count(objects), fp_a))
fp_a[[1]][c("Gal(b1-", "Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-")]
#>          Gal(b1- Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1- 
#>                3                2

Overlap counts: a Gal-Gal motif occurs twice in the three-Gal chain. Counts use glymotif’s strict substructure matching, including linkage and substituent labels. Symmetric mappings of the same residue set count once. Binary fingerprints are as.integer(count > 0). Reducing-end alpha/beta information is retained:

ends <- fp_motif_binary(c("Gal(a1-", "Gal(b1-"))
lapply(ends, function(x) x[c("Gal(a1-", "Gal(b1-")])
#> [[1]]
#> Gal(a1- Gal(b1- 
#>       1       0 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> Gal(a1- Gal(b1- 
#>       0       1

Fixed dictionary source and coverage

The built-in dictionary is glydb-2.12.1-complete-v1. It uses glydb 0.7.2.9000 at commit cafa287eac546a9899977a9e8c777af77cfd2ac3, whose structures come from GlyGen reviewed release 2.12.1. Of 49,728 parsed source records, 8,416 accessions pass complete-structure checks, representing 8,211 unique structures. The other 41,312 records are excluded. Exclusion reasons overlap: 31,654 uncertain reducing ends; 23,836 uncertain linkages; 6,218 floating parts; 4,443 alditols; 2,681 nonconcrete residues; 637 uncertain substituents; and 27 floating substituents. Before this step, glydb’s preparation excluded 10,266 parsing failures from 59,994 source records. Coverage therefore reflects that parser and source snapshot.

Connected motifs include branches and all sizes up to max_size, not just fragments of exactly that size. The dictionary contains 24,124 motifs with exact-size counts of 134, 906, 2,133, 3,110, 4,355, 5,849 and 7,637 for sizes 1–7. The default max_size = 3 selects 3,173 features and retains mono- and disaccharide information. Features are canonical strings sorted by UTF-8 bytes; no hashing or folding is used. Higher sizes can require more enumeration work.

The installed extdata/motif-dictionary-metadata.R records source and dictionary SHA-256 hashes, included-accession hash, exclusions and generator versions. The source repository’s data-raw/build-motif-dictionary.R reproduces the resource from the pinned glydb artifact. GlyGen database sets use CC BY 4.0; attribution and changes are recorded in the installed COPYRIGHTS file. The glydb package code is MIT licensed.

The connected-fragment design is informed by Glycan Fingerprints: Calculating Diversity in Glycan Libraries (2012) and its official supporting information. That paper uses 1–7-residue connected subtrees and hashed/folded binary strings; it does not supply this fixed explicit dictionary. glyfp does not reproduce its dataset-dependent occupancy correction or modified Tanimoto score.

With motif_dict = "fixed", an unseen motif never adds coordinates. unknown = "ignore" counts only known motifs; "warn" also warns and "error" rejects unseen motifs. This policy controls dictionary coverage, not uncertain input: unknown structural fields are always rejected. Different max_size values or dictionary versions define different coordinate sets. Save the method, options and glyfp version alongside results; recompute compared fingerprints after a dictionary change.

stopifnot(length(fp_motif_binary(character())) == 0L)
missing <- fp_motif_binary(NA_character_)[[1]]
stopifnot(length(missing) == 3173L, all(is.na(missing)))
path <- tempfile(fileext=".rds")
saveRDS(fp_a, path)
stopifnot(identical(readRDS(path), fp_a))
unlink(path)

Dynamic dictionaries

Set motif_dict = "dynamic" in either motif function to construct a dictionary from the non-missing glycans supplied in that call. It includes all connected motifs up to max_size, even if they are absent from the built-in glydb dictionary. Counting, binary thresholding and complete-structure validation are unchanged.

dynamic <- fp_motif_count(a, motif_dict = "dynamic")
dynamic[[1]]
#>                   Gal(b1-          Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1- Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1- 
#>                         3                         2                         1
stopifnot(identical(fp_motif_count(rev(a), motif_dict = "dynamic"), rev(dynamic)))
stopifnot(identical(fp_motif_binary(a, motif_dict = "dynamic"),
                   lapply(dynamic, function(x) 1L * (x > 0L))))

Each call rebuilds the dictionary, but it need not be different: batches with the same set of motifs produce the same dictionary. Unique canonical features are sorted by UTF-8 bytes, independent of input order and duplicates. Different batches may have different coordinates, including when vector lengths match. Combine all glycans to be compared in one call to ensure aligned dynamic coordinates:

combined <- fp_motif_count(c(a, b), motif_dict = "dynamic")
part_a <- combined[seq_along(a)]
part_b <- combined[length(a) + seq_along(b)]
stopifnot(identical(names(part_a[[1]]), names(part_b[[1]])))

unknown has no effect in dynamic mode because every extracted motif is included. It never permits uncertain structures. Empty input returns list(). An all-NA batch has an empty dictionary and returns one named zero-length integer vector per input; keep the original missingness mask because zero dimensions cannot represent NA. Missing entries in a mixed batch have all-NA vectors with that batch’s full dictionary. na_action = "error" rejects missing inputs in either mode. Dynamic mode does not change the bundled dictionary or later fixed calls.

Circular and residue-pair fingerprints

fp_circular_binary(), fp_circular_count() and fp_residue_pair() offer fixed-size, dictionary-free representations computed entirely in R. They need neither model weights nor a torch runtime. All default to n_bits = 2048. Use fp_circular_count() for circular occurrence counts, or mode = "count" with fp_residue_pair(). Inputs undergo the same complete-structure checks as motif methods. These methods retain the specified reducing-end state; they do not apply the embedding models’ root projection.

x <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", "Gal(b1-3)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
circular <- fp_circular_binary(x)
pairs <- fp_residue_pair(x)
stopifnot(identical(fp_circular_binary(x[1]), circular[1]))
stopifnot(identical(fp_residue_pair(rev(x)), rev(pairs)))
lengths(circular)
#> [1] 2048 2048 2048

Encoding rules

Circular encoding starts with each concrete residue label and its represented stereochemistry, positioned substituents, its own anomer/donor carbon, and a reducing-end flag. The root retains its explicit alpha/beta state. Each Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) round combines the previous label with a sorted multiset of neighbor messages: the neighbor label, full glycosidic linkage, and whether the center acts as donor or acceptor. The default radius = 2 records one feature per residue at each radius 0, 1 and 2. Repeated environments count repeatedly; radii are distinguished, even for single residues. Consequently count vectors sum to number_of_residues * (radius + 1).

Residue-pair encoding uses the same WL construction, with default radius = 1 for each endpoint. Only the final endpoint radius is used. Each distinct unordered pair contributes a feature consisting of its sorted endpoint labels and undirected shortest glycosidic-edge distance. All distances are included. This is graph distance, not 3D distance. Count vectors sum to n * (n - 1) / 2. No self-pairs are included, so all single-residue glycans have an all-zero residue-pair fingerprint; circular or motif features can distinguish them.

vapply(fp_circular_count(x[1:2]), sum, 0)
#> [1] 6 6
vapply(fp_residue_pair(x[1:2], mode = "count"), sum, 0)
#> [1] 1 1

Encoding version 1 packs fields as byte-length-prefixed UTF-8 strings, uses SHA-256 for WL labels and method-specific features, and reduces the first 32 bits of the final hash (big-endian) modulo n_bits. This avoids R serialization, random seeds and batch dictionaries. A bin accumulates every occurrence mapped to it; binary mode thresholds the final counts. Different features can collide. For example, n_bits = 1 maps every feature to the same bin. Increasing the vector length reduces folding collisions without recovering structural information omitted by the feature definition. Bin names record the method, version, radius, dimension and mode. Compare outputs only with the same settings and compatible package/dependency versions. Fixed hashing does not make fingerprints reversible or unique identifiers for glycans.

The bounded radius range is 0–10 and n_bits is 1–1,048,576. Radius counts graph edges, not the ECFP diameter convention. Circular environments can miss layout beyond their radius. Pair features add distances but omit the interior sequence of residues and linkage labels beyond their endpoint environments. With radius = 0, acceptor linkage positions are omitted by pair features. Absolute stereochemistry not represented in glyrepr labels is not reconstructed. Pair enumeration and its distance matrix require quadratic space in glycan size. Empty inputs return list(); missing inputs retain all n_bits entries as NA.

These are residue-level designs inspired by extended-connectivity fingerprints, WL graph kernels and atom-pair features, not exact atom-level ECFP, atom-pair or MAP4 implementations. Circular counts include every center at every radius; they do not deduplicate repeated subgraphs across radii.

Controlled comparison with motif features

The following small panel checks specific distinctions and failures. It is not a prediction benchmark or a claim of general superiority. Synthetic Gal/Man chains are used to control local motif content while changing longer-range layout; they are not asserted to be naturally occurring glycans. Motif counts use one dynamic dictionary per pair so coverage gaps in glydb do not confound the comparison. Hashed methods use count mode and their default radii and 2,048 bins. Results could change with these settings or folding collisions.

chain <- function(sequence) {
  residues <- ifelse(strsplit(sequence, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]] == "G", "Gal", "Man")
  paste0(paste(residues, collapse = "(b1-4)"), "(b1-")
}
panel <- list(
  linkage = c("Gal(b1-3)GlcNAc(b1-", "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-"),
  branches = c("Gal(b1-3)[GlcNAc(b1-6)]GalNAc(a1-",
               "Gal(b1-6)[GlcNAc(b1-3)]GalNAc(a1-"),
  reducing_end = c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(a1-", "Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-"),
  single_residue = c("Gal(b1-", "Man(b1-"),
  chain_8 = vapply(c("GGGMGGGG", "GGGGMGGG"), chain, ""),
  chain_20 = vapply(c("GGGGGGMGGGGGGGGGGGGG", "GGGGGGGMGGGGGGGGGGGG"), chain, "")
)
distinguishes <- function(x, encode) {
  values <- encode(x)
  !identical(values[[1]], values[[2]])
}
comparison <- data.frame(
  case = names(panel),
  motif_1_to_3 = vapply(panel, distinguishes, TRUE,
    encode = function(x) fp_motif_count(x, motif_dict = "dynamic")),
  circular_r2 = vapply(panel, distinguishes, TRUE,
    encode = function(x) fp_circular_count(x)),
  residue_pair_r1 = vapply(panel, distinguishes, TRUE,
    encode = function(x) fp_residue_pair(x, mode = "count"))
)
knitr::kable(comparison, row.names = FALSE)
case motif_1_to_3 circular_r2 residue_pair_r1
linkage TRUE TRUE TRUE
branches TRUE TRUE TRUE
reducing_end TRUE TRUE TRUE
single_residue TRUE TRUE FALSE
chain_8 FALSE TRUE TRUE
chain_20 FALSE FALSE TRUE

The 8-residue chains share the same counts of 1–3-residue motifs but differ in both hashed representations. The 20-residue chains also share the same local circular fingerprint at radius 2; endpoint distances separate this pair. In contrast, single-residue identity is lost entirely by the pair representation. These examples motivate combining complementary features when appropriate, while showing why no one of these representations guarantees structural identity.

Pretrained embeddings

All embedding methods use optional R torch on the CPU. Binary/count methods do not load torch or require a model runtime. Install the optional dependencies and runtime explicitly once; glyfp never installs them automatically:

install.packages(c("torch", "digest", "zip"))
torch::install_torch()

Input validation still requires a known reducing-end alpha/beta state. The pretrained models do not encode that state, so only after validation glyfp projects it out at the normal reducing carbon. Consequently, glycans differing only in reducing-end alpha/beta have identical embeddings but distinct motif fingerprints where the corresponding motifs are in the dictionary. Other reducing-end positions or unsupported chemistry produce errors. No other unknown structure is accepted or silently completed.

Under the same model, checkpoint, preprocessing and runtime settings, duplicate glycans, input order and batch size do not affect coordinates. CPU evaluation uses float32, frozen normalization, no dropout or gradients, and one graph per forward pass. Save the method, checkpoint identity and package/runtime versions with the resulting vectors. Different model versions define different spaces, even when lengths and coordinate names match. Cross-platform comparisons should allow floating-point tolerance; reference tests bound every coordinate’s absolute error by 1e-5. All-NA inputs retain the model’s full coordinate set.

SweetNet

SweetNet (2021) is a graph neural network over residues and linkages. fp_sweetnet() defaults to v2 and returns 128 coordinates from bn2(lin2(...)), before final activation, dropout and classification.

No environment variable or manual download is required for SweetNet. On first use, glyfp downloads the pinned official checkpoint, verifies SHA-256 and saves it in tools::R_user_dir("glyfp", "cache"). Subsequent calls verify and reuse it.

a <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", "GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
fp <- fp_sweetnet(a)
lengths(fp)
offline <- fp_sweetnet(a, download = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(fp, offline))
legacy <- fp_sweetnet(a, checkpoint = "sweetnet-v1")
Checkpoint Model
"sweetnet-v2" (default; about 3.82 MB) Residual graph layers with BatchNorm; mean and max pooling
"sweetnet-v1" Legacy glycowork 1.9.0 species model; three graph layers and mean pooling
Local .pt path Either supported official artifact, identified by its hash

Both versions return 128 coordinates, but their values must not be mixed. The v2 default follows the current upstream model, not a claim of better accuracy for every task. cache_dir changes the cache location; download = FALSE prevents network access and errors on an offline cache miss. A local file is never replaced or copied to a persistent cache:

fp <- fp_sweetnet(a,
  checkpoint = "/path/to/glycowork_sweetnet_species_v2.pt", download = FALSE)

Downloads use a temporary file, SHA-256 validation and atomic rename. Corrupt cache entries produce an error naming the file; remove that entry to permit a fresh download or supply a verified local file. Failed downloads leave no partial checkpoint to be mistaken for valid weights. Loading glyfp or using motif methods makes no network request. Original checkpoint files are never modified; legacy CUDA tags are relocated in a temporary CPU copy.

Supported MIT-licensed official artifacts:

  • SweetNet v2, SHA-256 bc3d901e4284554c1a245b8e6b7e291a5631c8932ca9c27eb8668b6d4424a146.
  • Legacy SweetNet, SHA-256 4ee19fc0593db0562c16585b556050694144816754750ebfe1876ed21ba0f4be.

Every residue/substituent/linkage token must be in the fixed vocabulary. Embedding functions always reject unknown tokens; no untrained token is used. The configurable unknown argument belongs only to motif functions.

GlycanGT

GlycanGT uses residue and linkage tokens in a graph Transformer. The supported large model trained with 35% node-and-edge masking returns its final 768-dimensional graph token.

Download its checkpoint yourself and supply a local path. glyfp never downloads GlycanGT weights. Obtain access under the conditions of the official model repository, then download outputs/mask_35/pretrained_tokengt_large_multitask_mask_35_final.pt (about 367 MB). The upstream project declares Apache-2.0; model access has a separate step. Do not put account credentials into R code.

fp <- fp_glycangt(
  c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", "Man(a1-3)[Man(a1-6)]Man(a1-"),
  checkpoint = "/path/to/pretrained_tokengt_large_multitask_mask_35_final.pt")
lengths(fp) # 768 768

The supported Hugging Face revision is 7c9f4a19b366ca48ed03995a0ad47fa1e745f24c, SHA-256 d490d18795ee6d4746b9b4abd0a5c733d8f7e4261998d050c1b741b65e530a54. Code follows the fixed official implementation. Omitting the local checkpoint or supplying a URL produces an error. fp_glycangt() has no download or cache_dir argument. Every call hashes the original file, even with tensors cached in memory. CUDA tags are relocated in a temporary CPU copy without changing the original file.

The official model generates orthogonal random node identifiers even in eval(). glyfp fixes one draw per canonical projected glycan: master seed 1729 plus a SHA-256-derived graph seed, the original single-graph Gaussian QR construction, and padding/truncation to width 64. Reducing-end alpha/beta is omitted before canonicalization and seed construction. Caller R and CPU torch RNG states are preserved. Upstream multi-graph batches use their maximum node count and may give different identifiers and outputs. This deterministic policy is not a claim to reproduce the paper’s downstream benchmark performance.

At least two residues and tokens in the fixed vocabulary are required; the upstream edge-triple pipeline does not retain edge-free graphs. Real pretrained reference comparisons cover 12 glycans and every coordinate under the same single-graph identifier policy, not the upstream stochastic multi-graph policy.

GIFFLAR

GIFFLAR combines atoms, bonds and residues through heterogeneous message passing. The R implementation follows the pinned glycowork network and graph builder. It concatenates three independent means into 384 coordinates, not the 1,076 classification scores. No Python, RDKit or GlyLES runtime is needed.

On first use, fp_gifflar() downloads glycowork_gifflar_species.pt (about 7.8 MB) from the official fixed revision. The code and model card declare MIT licensing. Downloads are verified before caching. SHA-256: 0dab7c3b61aad95dab37d4974da4b57b3fd985128dc09ad5da846e82adb9519d. Every call verifies it, including when tensors are already cached in memory. checkpoint = "gifflar-species" is the default. Use cache_dir to change the cache location and download = FALSE for offline use. Verified local paths are also accepted. Failed downloads leave no partial checkpoint; corrupt caches raise an error without being overwritten.

fp <- fp_gifflar(c("GlcNAc(b1-", "Gal6S(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_),
  checkpoint = "/path/to/glycowork_gifflar_species.pt")
lengths(fp) # 384 384 384

The native graph builder supports 27 fixed residue labels:

Group Residues
Unmodified Glc, Gal, Man, Fuc, Xyl, Rha, Rib, Ara
Amino and N-acetyl GlcN, GalN, GlcNAc, GalNAc, ManNAc
Uronic and sialic acids GlcA, GalA, IdoA, Neu5Ac, Neu5Gc, Kdn
Positioned sulfates Gal6S, GlcNAc6S, GlcNAc3S, GalNAc4S, GalNAc6S, IdoA2S
Positioned phosphates Glc6P, Man6P

Monosaccharides are supported. Other templates, anomeric-to-anomeric bonds and attachments that would move or extend a modification are rejected. For example, a child attached at position 2 of GlcN or position 6 of Glc6P is unsupported. There is no approximate molecular fallback. For short ambiguous text, use an explicit complete serialization such as Ara(a1- or an ecosystem parser.

The molecular graph retains official atom/chirality features, bond ownership, ring relations and both directions of linkage features. Bond order and charge are not separate input features in the official network. Atom, bond and residue means are pooled separately. No random identifiers are used. Graphs and real pretrained predictions have been checked against pinned upstream code on 86 structures covering every supported template and both linkage anomers.

Validation

Normal tests do not require network access. Small untrained networks validate ported operators independently of checkpoint access; they are not pretrained models. Real integration tests additionally use locally supplied files through developer-only variables GLYFP_TEST_CHECKPOINT, GLYFP_TEST_V2_CHECKPOINT, GLYFP_TEST_GLYCANGT_CHECKPOINT and GLYFP_TEST_GIFFLAR_CHECKPOINT. These tests cover numerical references, explicit complete input followed by the documented root projection, independent batches, duplicates, object/text equivalence, missingness, RNG preservation and unchanged original weight files.
